elements.text: Give urgent attention to the patient with breast symptoms and temperature ≥ 38°C or body pain with painful lump in breast/s which may be fluctuant: breast abscess likely.
Give paracetamol 1g and tramadol 50mg. Refer urgently to surgical unit for incision and drainage.
BREAST SYMPTOMS
1If penicillin allergy (history of anaphylaxis, urticaria or angioedema), give instead azithromycin 500mg daily for 3 days.

• Usually due to poor latching. Help to latch baby properly. • Avoid using soap on nipples. • Advise to apply breastmilk to nipples after feeding and expose to air. Apply zinc and castor oil ointment between feeds. Assess and manage baby for oral thrush.
Breastfeeding and painful/cracked nipples
Painful breast/s • Check for pregnancy 174. May be a side effect of hormonal contraception. If no better after 3 months, change contraceptive method 170. • If breast exam normal, mastalgia likely.

• Reassure this is common and advise a well-fitting bra. Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (max 4g/24 hours) for up to 5 days. • If symptoms change/worsen, refer to breast clinic/Regional Breast Unit within 60 days.

Nipple discharge • If pregnant and no other symptoms, reassure and give antenatal care 178. • Review medication: antipsychotics, antidepressants, COC and metoclopramide can cause nipple discharge. Discuss with doctor. • If cause uncertain, refer.
Breast lump/s Re-examine breast on day 7 of menstrual cycle. If lump persists, refer

Symptoms not related to breastfeeding

Axillary lump/s • Ask about other symptoms. If recent fever with cough/sore throat 23. If skin rash/itch 82. • If reactive node from infection or skin cause, manage as on symptom pages. Reassure that lymphadenopathy should resolve with treatment. • Review in 2-4 weeks. If lymph node persists, refer.

Breast enlargement • If only one breast enlarged, refer to breast clinic/Regional Breast Unit. • If BMI ≥ 25 156. • Review medication: antipsychotics, antidepressants, efavirenz, nifedipine, amlodipine can cause breast enlargement. Discuss with doctor. If on efavirenz, doctor to consider switch to dolutegravir 132.
Is the patient breastfeeding?

Yes. Mastitis likely • Give flucloxacillin1 500mg 6 hourly for 5 days. • Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed up to 5 days. • Advise warm compresses. If no better after 2 days or breast abscess develops, refer same day.
No. Engorgement/blocked

duct likely • Advise frequent breastfeeds, warm compresses and to gently massage breast. • Advise to return if fever/body pain (mastitis) develops. • If symptoms persists, consider other causes and discuss/refer.
Refer to breastfeeding counsellor/lactation consultant or support group. If HIV positive, give routine HIV care 126 and prevent transmission to baby 186.
Breastfeeding and painful breast/s with or without lump/s
Does patient have temperature ≥ 38°C or body pain?

• If HIV negative, advise to continue breastfeeding. • If HIV positive and only one breast affected, express and discard milk from affected side. Continue breastfeeding from other side. - If both breasts affected, temporarily stop feeding from breasts, express and discard breast milk. Replace feeds with formula until cracks/mastitis resolved.

Approach to the patient with breast symptoms not needing urgent attention Carefully examine both breasts including nipples and axillae. If any of the following warning signs, refer to breast clinic/Regional Breast Unit same week: • Skin changes: dimpling, ulceration, indentations or pulling ("orange peel" appearance) • Breast lump/s with any of: patient > 25 years, family history of breast cancer, irregular fixed lump, skin/nipple changes, nipple discharge, axillary lump

• Axillary lump/s with any of: skin/nipple changes, nipple discharge, breast lump/s • Nipple discharge/retraction with any of: patient ≥ 50 years, blood-stained or one-sided discharge, male, skin changes (crusts/ulcers), breast/axillary lump If none of above, continue to assess the patient below:
